newsitem.title: UK: Market expectations of broad EMU rise - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Market expectations of broad EMU rise - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad- based European Monetary Union, including peripheral countries like Italy, Spain and Sweden, rose further over the past week, JP Morgan's EMU calculator showed.
The U.S. investment house's method of calculating market expectations of EMU taking place monitors bond yield spreads in the swaps market between participating European countries.

The latest calculations show that the market's probability in Italy participating in EMU rose 4.0 percentage points to 69 percent in the five trading days to Wednesday, while perceived EMU probability in Spain rose 6.0 points to 79 percent. Sweden was up three points to 74 percent.
EMU expectations in these three countries have shown a steady rise over the past 20 days, with Spain's probability up 24 points over that period, Sweden up 16 points and Italy up seven points.

"The latest numbers suggest the market has become very optimistic over the prospect of a stability pact at the forthcoming (EU) summit," said Avinash Persaud, head of currency research at JP Morgan in Europe.
Elsewhere, perceived probability levels in the U.K. rose 2.0 points to 42 percent over the last week, but were up 12 points in the last 20 days.
According to these calculations, the market still believes there is a 100-percent chance of France and Belgium being in EMU and that was unchanged from last week.

The calculator works by assigning a market probability level to each country. This is derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
